the major maintenance procedures 
P1, which must be carried out on an annually 
bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block.

 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable 
 safety category,

Safety fence

items:
A work permit 
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable 
 safety category,
Circuit breaker must be out of service.
Work must be done in a clean area or in workshop.
Make sure that the breaker is open.

Close and open the breaker to make sure that the opening and closing
 spring are released before starting work.
One set of metric open end box wrenches size range 13 mm to 24 mm.

Adjustable spanner - One set of screwdrivers -Torque wrench - Fine
 file-Fine emery cloth -Wipers
Complete set of gaskets for the circuit breaker.
One barrel of new oil (its dielectric strength not less than 40 kV/2.5).
Dielectric strength oil tester.
Some of gasoline, lubricating oil and grease.
Clean pails for changing oil.
Tin cans to hold bolts, nuts, studs, washers etc.

Do not throw any oil into the sewage because the oil prevent the sewage
 treatment process.

Collect the oil that drained out of the poles into a barrel and return it
 back to the vendor to recycle it to save money.

Collect the oil used in washing the poles in another barrel and do not
 re-use it for filling the poles unless filtered, dried and its dielectric
 strength measured with an oil tester (not less than 40kV/2.5 mm).
Do not burn cloth used in cleaning but collect it and send it to the dump.

Types
 (M12-25-12SE AND 2M12-20-8)

items:
Unscrew the screw (20 fig. 3) of the insulating cover of the fixed
 contact. Use screwdriver
Take off the insulating cylinder (21 fig 3).
Inspect the fixed contact elements and the contact springs:

If the contact elements and contact springs are in good condition and
 not deteriorated, clean them with new oil and clean cloth, then reassemble
 the fixed contact as follow:
Place the insulating cylinder (21 fig 3) to the porter of contact.
Fit the screw (20 fig 3) to fix the insulating cylinder (21 fig 3).

If any element of the 
fixed contact is deteriorated, the replacement can be performed as follow:

items:
Unscrew the screw (51fig 3) and pull out the tress (52 fig 3) from the
 porter of the fixed contact (53 fig 3).

Replace the deteriorated elements, if there are only some pittings on
 the contacts fingers, it is necessary to file them by fine file without
 modifying the profile of elements and then clean out fillings and clean
 the fixed contact with new oil.

If there are more than one of contact fingers are deteriorated, remove
 the two springs of fixed contact to disassemble the fingers and change it.
 Use screwdriver

To the porter of the contact (No 53) fit a spring connected with the
 hooks in a ring.
Fit the two stars (No 55).

Place the long contact finger (No 56) under the spring (No 54), taking
 care that the tress (No 52) enter in the groove of the porter of the fixed
 contact (No 53).
Place the other contact fingers with the same method.
Pull over the other spring (No 54) connected with the hooks in a ring.

Fasten the tress (No 52) to the porter (No 53) with the screw (No 51)
 and washer (No 57).
Subsequent operation under item 1.

During replacement take care not to deteriorate the thin membrane on the
 porter (53)

Inspection of moving contact is not necessary unless a remarkable
 deterioration is observed on fixed contact. If necessary the inspection of
 moving contact is to be made as follow:
Make sure that the breaker is open.

Drain the oil out by removing the oil drain plug (14 fig 2) and allow
 the oil to drain out of pole into a container placed under each pole.
Remove the screws fixing the insulating cylinder to oil sump.

Lift the insulating cylinder and lay it gently on a clean board, take
 care not to damage the lower face.
If the tip of the contact rod is badly deteriorated it must be replaced.

After operation described in previous item are carried out, the following
 additional operations are to be carried out:

items:
Unscrew the nuts (25 fig 4) from the opening spring (one nut is left
 screwing).

The opening spring rotate manually in the direction to the poles until
 lost the force.

Remove the ring (27 fig 4) then the pin (26 fig 4) with a needle nose
 plier.

With a spanner with a mouth 27mm gently rotate the main shaft (28 fig4)
 in the direction of the closing of the circuit breaker (in
 anti-clockwise). When the contact rod is lifted and the upper side of the
 lever (63 fig 5) is out of the oil sump the rotation should be stopped.
 Then the guide and the conical shock absorber (61 fig 5) should be lifted,
 take care that the angle on the shaft of the oil sump is maximum 45o (see
 fig 5).

With a needle-nose plier remove one ring (64 fig5) and pull out the pin
 (65 fig5).

Replace the moving contact complete (12 fig5) and the gasket for oil
 sump (66 fig5) if needed.
On the new moving contact put the guide and shock absorber (61 fig 5).

Connect the lever (62 fig 5) and the moving contact with the pin (65 fig
 5 ) and fit the ring (64 fig 5) with the special pincer rotate the main
 shaft in clock-wise up to the open position of the moving contact

Fit the pin ( 26 fig 4) in the holes on the frame and on the opening
 spring and place the ring (27 fig 4) with special pincer, the opening
 spring (24 fig 4) rotate in the direction to the operating mechanism until
 the dimension 207 mm ( see fig 4).

Tighten the nuts (25 fig 4 ) of the opening spring and then reassemble
 the poles.

Unscrew the special nut (29 fig 2) of the lower terminal by the special
 spanner.

Tighten the two nuts (30 fig 2) one with other and turning
 anti-clockwise remove the lower terminal from the guiding contact
 complete.

Pull out the guiding contact complete with the arc chamber out of the
 insulating cylinder.

Inspect the arc chamber, the dimension (a) should be maximum 32mm (see
 fig 6).

If the arc chambers are not deteriorated clean them with clean oil and
 clean wipers then locate with the guiding contact in the insulating
 cylinder.

Tighten the lower terminal in the guiding contact with the nuts (30 fig
 2).
Tighten the special nut (29 fig 2) by the special spanner.

Clean the surfaces of the pole and oil sump, then locate the insulating
 cylinder after changing its gasket and tighten the screws fixing it to the
 oil sump.
Unscrew the screw (72).

In the guiding contact complete place a new arc chamber (10 fig 2), and
 if necessary a new gasket (73).
The further operations are the same in item 6.

The fixed contact (9) locate in the insulating cylinder and turn until
 the long contact finger enter in the opening of the arc chamber (when the
 fixed contact is in the right position, the upper terminal is about 60 mm
 above the insulating cylinder).

On the upper terminal place a star with the scored side in down
 direction, taking care that the arms of the star enter in the groves.
Place the locking nut (19) and with the special spanner easy tighten.
Refill the poles with fresh oil to wash the three poles.
Close the breaker.
Tighten the locking nut (19).
Open the breaker.
Fit the insulating cover (7) with a gasket.
With the special spanner tighten nut (18).
Close and open the breaker two times then drain the oil out.
Refill the three poles with new oil for operation.

sections.text:
As the dealing experience with this Type of circuit breakers we find that it
 can undergo four opening operations at short circuit without replacing oil ,
 but you have to replace oil after five short circuit as follows:

items:
Before starting drainage the oil out of the poles be sure that the
 breaker is in open position, then remove the outlet plug (14 fig 2) and
 allow all oil to drain out of poles into a container replaced under each
 pole.

Close the outlet plugs, open the filling plugs at the top of each pole
 and pour oil into each pole.

After oil has reached the oil level indicators (6 fig 2) close and trip
 the breaker three times to wash the arc chambers, and contacts.
Remove the outlet plugs and allow all oil to drain out of the poles.
Repeat the previous steps until you find the drainage oil be cleaned.

Refill the poles with oil of dielectric strength not less than 30 kV/mm
 , during the filling the breaker must be in open position and oil must be
 poured slowly into each pole till the right mark on the oil level
 indicators.

Wait a few minutes and if the oil level has lowered, fill up to the
 right mark.

sections.text:
All mechanical test operations must be carried only when the 3 poles are
 filled with oil.

items:
Before putting the CB into service, it is necessary to carry out some
 hand closing and opening operations to make sure that the operating
 mechanism works satisfactorily and carry out some electrical closing and
 opening operations to make sure that connection are right and that the
 closing mechanism operates satisfactorily.

For hand closing operation, insert the detachable crank (15 fig.2) into
 its place and manually rotate the main shaft in clock-wise until the free
 rotation of the shaft, the state of springs is indicated by a colored
 indicator on the cover of the operating mechanism. (Red: spring
 loaded-white: spring released), then turn the closing crank (16 fig 2) in
 clock-wise (to direction of the mark "1". The state of the
 breaker is indicated by a colored indicator on the cover of the operating
 mechanism (red: breaker closed - white: breaker released).

To trip the breaker turn the closing crank (16 fig 2) in anti -clockwise
 (to the direction of the mark "O"
Check that the releases trip the breaker satisfactorily.
Check that the auxiliary switch works satisfactorily.

If closing springs are released, the motor when energized loads the
 sprigs and stops automatically as soon as springs are fully loaded.

If the breaker works with series releases, adjust the trip setting of
 releases.

Clean the mechanism parts by means of a paint brush drenched with diesel
 oil and petrol, be sure that the breaker is open and springs are released
 before starting cleaning

Clean the metal parts by means of a clean dry duster and clean the
 insulating parts by means of another dry duster.

After making sure that the operating mechanism is in good working
 condition and that the pole are filled with oil at the right level, the
 breaker can be put into service.

Finally record all that has been done on the maintenance card of the
 circuit breaker.
